headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap in n8n can cascade into prompt injection and data leakage when paired with langchain4j.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read and write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools, so attacker-controlled content can enter workflows and be treated as instructions. langchain4j is an LLM orchestration library with no documented isolation or provenance controls in the profile. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflow setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest untrusted file or API content and pass it to langchain4j prompts
IF no provenance or instruction/content separation is added between n8n nodes and langchain4j
mitigations: Add explicit prompt delimiters in workflow templates
Reject untrusted file content before prompt assembly
Tag workflow inputs with provenance metadata
Use a fixed system prompt that ignores embedded instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress, filesystem access, and per-credential secret handling; it can process whatever the workflow touches. langchain4j has no network egress in its profile, but it can still receive sensitive workflow data from n8n and surface it in outputs. The shared data path exists in default orchestration, so leakage risk is material.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process secrets, customer data, or files and forward them into langchain4j prompts
IF workflow outputs are logged or sent to external integrations
mitigations: Minimize fields passed from n8n to langchain4j
Mask secrets before prompt construction
Disable verbose workflow logging
Restrict credential scopes per node
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses, while langchain4j is an LLM library that may also operate on files or generated artifacts in the same workflow. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so concurrent writes or shell-driven side effects can collide on shared state. Uncertainty about exact shared paths pushes this upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF n8n Execute Command or Code nodes mutate files that langchain4j also reads or writes
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable Execute Command for shared paths
Use immutable handoff artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is explicitly a multi-agent orchestrator with AI Agent nodes and tool-use patterns, so it can treat upstream outputs as actionable workflow inputs. langchain4j can generate model outputs that n8n may route into downstream nodes without verification. That creates a default cascade from generated text to automated actions, with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF n8n routes langchain4j output into action nodes without a validation step
IF generated text is used as structured parameters for emails, tickets, or API calls
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action nodes
Validate model output against a schema
Require confidence thresholds for automation
Log and review rejected outputs
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between nodes

E_compliance.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and stores secrets in its server credential store, while langchain4j is a general-purpose LLM library with no residency or retention controls documented in the profile. If regulated data flows through n8n into LLM prompts or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined data path.
conditions: IF workflows process regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or customer secrets
IF n8n logs, stores, or forwards that data to external services
mitigations: Classify data before workflow execution
Block regulated fields from LLM prompts
Set retention limits on workflow logs
Review credential and backup retention settings
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
